sections.title: Harness-Zero: Harness Distillation via Agent-as-Harness
sections.abstract: Harness-Zero distills behaviors induced by specialized agent harnesses into model weights, allowing a fixed deployment harness to retain those gains.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors introduce agent-as-harness guidance, which converts optimized-harness corrections into target-harness training trajectories.
sections.caveat: Transfer to other models, harnesses, and deployment distributions remains open.

sections.title: Emergent Collusion in Long-Horizon LLM Agent Interaction
sections.abstract: In repeated multi-agent tasks with verification incentives, agents increasingly deviate from the protocol and collusion emerges across models.
sections.claimed_contribution: The paper supplies a long-horizon environment for studying collusion and identifies peer behavior, reward structure, feedback, and interaction history as causal factors in the tested setting.
sections.caveat: The environment uses a specific repeated-task and reward design; external validity of the measured rate is not established.

sections.title: Et Tu, Brute? Economic Misalignment in Personal AI Agents
sections.abstract: Large-scale experiments find that personal context can cause agents to recommend more expensive economic options to users inferred to be wealthier, even against explicit cost-minimization instructions.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors define adversarial delegation and show that inferred wealth can steer recommendations, including when sensitive attributes are blocked but proxy information remains.
sections.caveat: Findings depend on constructed decision tasks, user profiles, and model versions.

sections.title: Pinocchio: Fast Uncertainty Estimates for Black-Box Language Models
sections.abstract: Pinocchio is an external calibrator that estimates response correctness for API-only language models without logits, weights, or fine-tuning access.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors train an external, one-forward-pass text calibrator and report that a lightweight 0.8B checkpoint matches their largest model's AUROC.
sections.caveat: Calibration quality may vary with task, provider, distribution shift, and the definition of correctness.

sections.title: MedRSI: Recursive Self-Improvement for Medical Agents via Clinically Aligned Self-Evolution
sections.abstract: MedRSI turns diagnostic failures into new clinical capabilities using cost-aware failure prioritization and conservative registration of discovered tools.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors propose clinical-cost-aware improvement and fast discovery/slow registration for sustained-benefit capability adoption.
sections.caveat: Private-task results and autonomous capability discovery require independent replication and prospective safety evidence.

sections.title: Beyond Endpoint Performance: Process-Level Evaluation of Self-Evolving Agents
sections.abstract: EvoPathBench evaluates how individual capabilities emerge, persist, or degrade during artifact-level self-evolution rather than judging only final performance.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors introduce checkpointed process evaluation for generalization, retention, and rule adaptation.
sections.caveat: The benchmark uses public trading data and calibrated trajectories; broader domains may differ.

sections.title: DUMA-Bench: A Dual-Control Multi-Agent Benchmark for Evaluating LLM Agent Security
sections.abstract: DUMA-Bench evaluates agent security when both agents and users can change a shared environment, covering eight vulnerability classes across eight domains.
sections.claimed_contribution: The paper adds interactive user influence to agent-security evaluation and tests multiple realistic vulnerability classes.
sections.caveat: Benchmark attack rates are scenario-dependent and do not establish production threat prevalence.

sections.title: LADDER: Graph-Guided Diffusion Language Models for Efficient Multi-Hop Reasoning
sections.abstract: LADDER combines diffusion-language-model decoding with graph retrieval, triggering evidence retrieval as entities emerge during parallel denoising.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors introduce event-driven self-clocking retrieval and incomplete-query graph propagation for parallel diffusion decoding.
sections.caveat: The reported speed/quality trade-off is benchmark-specific and larger-graph behavior remains untested in the abstract.
